messages:
maria: heads up — noticed steady memory growth in kv-cache during the 20k-token long-context soak (private test farm). p50 OK but resident memory climbs over time. attaching quick profiling summary and flamegraph link -> https://ci.redwood/test/kv-flame-1758 :frowning:

maria: main observations: 1) allocation counts for 64/128B bins steadily increase, 2) compaction events are rare, 3) paging shows lots of small free fragments that never coalesce

devin: ugh. which build? any recent allocator changes or kernel selection tweaks in the last deploy?

maria: build: runtime-v1.42.2+opt-batch. we rolled the kernel tweak for attention tiling a few days ago; not sure that should affect kv allocator but trying to correlate.

sam: can you paste the `kv-stats` dump (the /debug endpoint)? small buckets exploding smells like binning thresholds misaligned for our typical kv pair sizes.

anika: I ran a microbench on master vs v1.42.2 — short summary: master has slightly lower tail latency but v1.42.2 shows 8% more allocations in the 64B bin under longcontext replay. full output:```
# kv-stats snapshot
total_allocs: 1_234_567
bin[32]: 12k
bin[64]: 412k
bin[128]: 310k
free_fragments: 29k
compactions: 18
page_faults: 420
```

anika: result from the compaction experiment (local): enabling mini-compact every 5s reduced resident by ~12% but increased tail latency by ~30ms under peak token pump.

liam: I think two levers: 1) binning tweaks (grow 64->96 split or widen 64 bin to avoid churn), 2) more aggressive background compactor but with latency-aware preemption.

liam: quick patch I prototyped — change allocator bins from [32,64,128] to [32,48,80,128] and add jittered compaction window:
```
# allocator.conf
small_bins: [32,48,80,128]
mini_compact_interval_ms: 3500..7000 # jitter
max_compact_jobs: 1
latency_preempt_threshold_ms: 20
```

devin: nice. did you simulate long-context streaming (20k tokens)? compaction spike could tickle the scheduler and add tail latency.

liam: yes, ran 2x parallel longcontext streams for 30m. resident drop ~11% and 95p latency increase ~28ms at compaction events. but average latency unaffected.

sam: That matches an expected tradeoff. Maybe instead of full compaction we do selective coalesce for contiguous free ranges > 512B so we avoid touching too many pages at once.

maria: selective coalesce sounds promising. Also noticed kernel selection heuristic changes increased batching sizes slightly which increases KV cache working set per request; that could amplify fragmentation because we hold longer-lived cache entries.

anika: FWIW I profiled allocation lifetimes — a lot of entries are medium-lived (hundreds of ms to seconds). They tend to fragment small bins when mixed with ephemeral allocations from beamsearch. Suggest heuristics to segregate medium-lived items into a 'long-slab' pool.

sam: segregation is low-risk: a second allocator arena for long-lived kv entries. When an entry's lifespan > threshold move it to the long-slab which uses larger chunk sizes and less frequent compaction.

maria: +1. telemetry wise we need to emit histograms for bin churn rate, longest-free-run sizes, and compaction latency to evaluate.

devin: also flag to check: did the attention-kernel change modify max prefix caching size? if more KV gets kept per request, reuse patterns change and that can increase small holes. I'll diff the kernel PR.

liam: quick note: we saw 'stale tail' phenomenon where free fragments stay fragmented because eviction policy avoids touching them — consider an eviction-triggered local compaction when eviction fails to reclaim enough contiguous pages.

ops-bot: Deploy queued: kv-alloc-experiments -> canary (3 nodes) by liam. ETA ~5m. :rocket:

maria: perfect — can we run the long-context soak against the canary with `mini-compact` enabled and binning patch? please add `emit:kv-churn` to canary metrics.

liam: will do. also adding a toggle for selective-coalesce so we can A/B it.

anika: I'll prepare the dashboards and an eval prompt set to detect regressions in tail token generation latency.

devin: if the canary shows the same memory growth, next step: instrument stack traces for allocations (sampling) to find code paths allocating medium bins.

maria: action items: 1) canary deploy with new bins + jittered compactor + `kv-churn` metrics (liam), 2) dashboard and eval harness (anika), 3) allocation sampling enabled if regression persists (devin), 4) design long-slab arena proposal (sam). I'll open a tracking issue. :thumbsup:

liam: opened issue #INF-7845 and linked canary logs.

maria: thanks all — will report back after 2h soak.
